title: Date, Time, and Timestamps with Time Zones
description: Master TIMESTAMPTZ vs TIMESTAMP, INTERVAL arithmetic, AT TIME ZONE conversion, and ISO 8601 formatting.

data.text: Handling timestamps correctly is essential for distributed applications. PostgreSQL provides two primary timestamp representations: **`TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE`** and **`TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` (`TIMESTAMPTZ`)**.

When you store a value into `TIMESTAMPTZ`, PostgreSQL converts it from your client's local timezone into **UTC** and stores the UTC epoch physically in 8 bytes. When querying, it converts the UTC timestamp back to the requesting client's timezone setting. `TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE` completely discards timezone offsets, causing horrific bugs during Daylight Saving Time transitions!

data.title: Date Arithmetic with INTERVAL
data.code:
-- Adding intervals to current time
SELECT 
    NOW() AS current_time_utc,
    NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days' AS thirty_days_ago,
    NOW() + INTERVAL '2 hours 15 minutes' AS future_time,
    -- Converting timezone explicitly
    NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York' AS new_york_time;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: PostgreSQL stores `TIMESTAMPTZ` in UTC internally and converts to client timezone dynamically.
Use `INTERVAL` for clean time addition and subtraction.
